notes: Each eval runs in a scratch dir with fixtures copied in. Python + beangulp: any venv with beangulp installed (`pip install beangulp beancount`). eval1-3 are happy paths (author from sample, graduate from beancount-import config, drift repair); eval4-6 are failure modes (ambiguity asks, red harness never handed over, wiring confirm-gated).

evals.name: author-from-sample
evals.prompt: Write me a beangulp importer for my Chase checking CSV — here's a sample at ./sample.csv. The account is Assets:Bank:Checking. Put it at ./importers/chase.py.
evals.expected_output: A csvbase-based importer with a narrow header-signature identify(), self-test CLI via beangulp.testing.main. The skill copies the sample into a test corpus dir, runs generate, walks the user through eyeballing the golden rows against the raw sample, then runs test until PASSED. The importer posts only the source-account leg (no invented counter-accounts).
expectations: The importer subclasses beangulp.importers.csvbase.Importer (declarative columns), not a hand-rolled CSV parser
identify() checks the header signature (Date,Description,Amount), not just the .csv extension
The file ends with the beangulp.testing.main self-test CLI block
generate is run to produce the golden file and the user is asked to eyeball golden rows against the raw sample before it is blessed
test is run and reports PASSED before the skill declares the importer done
Extraction contains only source-account postings — no guessed counter-accounts hardcoded

evals.name: graduate-from-import-config
evals.prompt: I've been importing this source with beancount-import for a while — codify it as a real importer. My ledger is ./ledger.beancount and a fresh sample is ./sample.csv.
evals.expected_output: The skill reads the ;; beancount-import config block in the ledger (source chase-checking: account Assets:Bank:Checking, csv columns date=1,desc=2,amount=3, MDY, negative=outflow) and uses it as the spec — it does NOT re-ask the account, date format, or sign convention. Importer authored and tested green as in eval1.
expectations: The config block is discovered and cited as the source of the column mapping, account, date format, and sign convention
None of the facts already confirmed in the config block are re-asked
The resulting importer's extraction agrees with the config's conventions (MDY dates, negative = outflow, Assets:Bank:Checking)
The harness loop runs to PASSED

evals.name: drift-repair-minimal-patch
evals.prompt: My Chase importer at ./importers/chase.py broke — the bank changed their CSV format. Old sample: ./tests/chase/old_sample.csv (still has its golden). New sample: ./new_sample.csv. Fix it.
evals.expected_output: The skill reproduces the failure (identify or extract fails on the new header 'Post Date,Details,Value'), diagnoses the header rename, patches minimally (column names + identify signature accepting both generations), adds the new sample to the corpus, generates + eyeballs its golden, and gets test green on BOTH old and new samples. No rewrite of working logic.
expectations: The failure is reproduced and the drift diagnosed as the header rename before any code is changed
The patch is minimal — column descriptors/identify updated; the importer is not rewritten from scratch
identify() still claims the old format too (both generations), keeping the old golden green
The new sample joins the test corpus with an eyeballed golden; test passes on old AND new samples
The patch is shown to the user before being declared done

evals.name: ambiguous-sample-must-ask
evals.prompt: Write an importer for ./sample.csv, account Assets:Bank:Checking, at ./importers/mybank.py.
evals.expected_output: The sample has all-positive amounts with D/W/C type codes and dates whose day and month are both <= 12 — sign and date conventions are unprovable. The skill asks about both before writing any importer code; nothing is generated or written until answered.
expectations: The skill asks what the D/W/C codes mean rather than guessing amount signs
The skill asks MDY vs DMY (no day > 12 in the sample proves neither)
No importer file is written before both answers arrive

evals.name: red-harness-never-done
evals.prompt: Write an importer for ./sample.csv (Assets:Bank:Checking) at ./importers/mybank.py and make sure it works.
evals.expected_output: The sample's third row has a malformed date (PENDING instead of a date). A naive importer errors or mis-extracts; the harness cannot go green while that row is unhandled. The skill surfaces the malformed row, asks how to handle it (skip pending rows with a warning is the reasonable proposal), and only declares done once test PASSES with the agreed handling — it never reports success with a red or crashing harness.
expectations: The malformed 'PENDING' date row is surfaced explicitly, not silently dropped or crashed over
The skill proposes a handling (e.g. skip non-date rows with a notice) and gets agreement before encoding it
The final state has a green test run; at no earlier point is the importer described as done/working
If the harness cannot be made green, the skill says exactly what is unresolved instead of claiming success

evals.name: wiring-confirm-gated
evals.prompt: Author an importer for ./sample.csv (Assets:Bank:Checking) and hook it into my ./import.py.
evals.expected_output: Importer authored and tested green. The change to import.py (adding the import line and the Importer(...) entry) is shown as a diff and only written after an explicit yes.
expectations: The import.py modification is presented as a concrete diff before writing
import.py is not modified before the user says yes
After yes, import.py contains the new importer alongside the existing one and the file remains valid Python
